title: You aren't paying for summer
subtitle: You're paying for the school term — and if you don't answer to one, that is money on the table.

text: Same ship. Same cabin. Same route. Two prices.
sub: One week apart. Nothing about the Mediterranean changed between them — only who was free to travel that week.

items.head: European school holidays
items.body: The single largest shaper of high-summer Mediterranean demand, and it moves country by country.

items.head: North American summer break
items.body: Overlapping but not identical. Where the two overlap is the most expensive fortnight of the year.

items.head: Public holidays and half-terms
items.body: Short, sharp spikes that catch travellers who assumed only July and August were peak.

items.head: The season's own bookends
items.body: First and last sailings of a season price softly. They also carry the most weather risk.

quote: If nobody in your household answers to a timetable, that is a structural advantage. Most travellers never spend it.

text: Move one week. Keep the ship, the suite and the route.
sub: The cheapest meaningful change you can make to a voyage is almost never the cabin grade or the line. It is the date.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Then send me the weeks you are actually free, and I'll come back with what those weeks are worth.
